narr: An upper level low was located directly over the region on June 9th. Daytime heating, a moist atmosphere in place and instability aloft allowed for thunderstorm development during the afternoon hours. A cluster of storms developed across southeast New Hampshire and dropped very heavy rain in a localized area of Rockingham County.
ev: A cluster of thunderstorms moved over Salem between 3 and 430 pm. An unofficial weather station recorded rainfall up to 4.25 inches in the area with instantaneous rates peaking around 4 inches per hour. The rapid runoff over this urban area resulted in a foot of water on Route 28, disrupting the evening commuter traffic.
lsr: Video from social media of up to 1 foot of water on rt 28.
